title: Acts Bible Quiz - Chapter 23
description: Ten questions on Acts 23: Paul before the council, the plot of more than forty men, and the night ride to Caesarea.

questions.text: Who commanded those standing by to strike Paul on the mouth?
questions.explanation: Acts 23:2 says the high priest, Ananias, commanded those who stood by him to strike him on the mouth.

answers.text: Felix the governor
The commanding officer
The high priest, Ananias
One of the centurions

questions.text: What did Paul call the man who had ordered him to be struck?
questions.explanation: Paul said, "God will strike you, you whitewashed wall!" and asked why he was struck contrary to the law.

answers.text: A whitewashed wall
A blind guide
A thief of the temple
A son of the devil

questions.text: What did Paul cry out that he was, when he saw the two parties in the council?
questions.explanation: Paul cried out that he was a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees, and that he was being judged concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead.

answers.text: A Sadducee, a son of Sadducees
A scribe of the law
A soldier of Rome
A Pharisee, a son of Pharisees

questions.text: What do the Sadducees say, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The chapter explains that the Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit, while the Pharisees confess all of these.

answers.text: That the law was given by angels alone
That there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit
That only the priests will rise again
That the prophets were not sent by God

questions.text: What did the Lord tell Paul when he stood by him the following night?
questions.explanation: The Lord told Paul to cheer up, because as he had testified about him at Jerusalem, so he must testify also at Rome.

answers.text: That he must testify also at Rome
That he would be set free the next day
That he would never see Jerusalem again
That he would sail to Cyprus to preach

questions.text: What did more than forty men bind themselves under a curse to do?
questions.explanation: They bound themselves under a curse to neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul, and there were more than forty of them.

answers.text: Keep silent until Paul had left the city
Fast for forty days in the temple
Neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul
Pay the high priest for Paul's death

questions.text: Who heard of the ambush and went into the barracks to tell Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul's sister's son heard that they were lying in wait, and he came and entered the barracks and told Paul.

answers.text: The high priest Ananias
Paul's sister's son
A scribe of the Pharisees
One of the elders of the Jews

questions.text: What did the commanding officer order his two centurions to prepare for the journey to Caesarea?
questions.explanation: He told them to prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred men armed with spears, at the third hour of the night.

answers.text: Seventy soldiers with spears and two chariots of war
Two hundred horsemen and twelve guards of the temple
A single centurion with ten soldiers of the barracks
Two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen

questions.text: Who wrote the letter to the governor Felix about Paul?
questions.explanation: The letter begins, "Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings."

answers.text: Claudius Lysias
Ananias the high priest
Julius the centurion
Tertullus the orator

questions.text: Where did the governor command that Paul be kept?
questions.explanation: After saying he would hear Paul fully when his accusers arrived, the governor commanded that he be kept in Herod's palace.

answers.text: In the barracks at Jerusalem
In the temple courts
In Herod's palace
On a ship bound for Rome
